mission_assessment.heart: authorized peer-to-peer folder convergence under evidence-bound local truth
mission_assessment.rev0696_focus: reopen abandoned or quarantined resume-transfer workorders only through an explicit terminal-reset event that preserves previous terminal evidence and current plan evidence

audit_refactor_target: terminal resume-transfer workorder boundary, reset event schema, and reset option/result API surface
audit_findings: Rev0695 made abandoned and quarantined rows durable terminal safety facts, but the only recovery path was out-of-band SQLite mutation or leaving work permanently stopped.
Ordinary reclaim/execution should remain fail-closed against terminal states; repair should be a separate API, not a weakening of claim/reclaim.
A reset decision must preserve prior worker, lease, retry, attempt, staging, and idempotency evidence beside the new current transfer-plan evidence before the row becomes claimed again.
behavioral_invariants_added: terminal reset requires at least one explicit terminal-state permission: reset_abandoned_workorders or reset_quarantined_workorders
quarantined rows cannot be silently reclaimed; they reopen only through a reset event
abandoned rows cannot be reset when stored workorder evidence no longer matches the current transfer plan
reset event insert happens before the terminal workorder row is updated back to work_state='claimed'
reset rows receive a fresh worker, lease, claimed_at_epoch, lease_expires_at_epoch, retry_at_epoch, and current execution idempotency key
existing reclaim, abandon, and quarantine history remains queryable after reset
